record.context_brief: Fourier support of Schwartz class orthonormal wavelets
record.original_question:
Let ψ ∈ L2(R) be an orthonormal wavelet as in the dyadic definition, and assume ψ belongs to the Schwartz class (the collection of all ∞-regular functions).

Is the Fourier transform ψ̂ necessarily compactly supported?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$. We say that $\psi$ is an orthonormal wavelet (with respect to the dyadic dilation) if the family
$$\psi_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2}\psi(2^j x - k), \qquad j,k \in \mathbb{Z},$$
forms an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.

Recall that the Schwartz class $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ is the space of all $C^\infty$ functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that for every pair of nonnegative integers $m,n$,
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}} |x|^m \,|f^{(n)}(x)| < \infty.$$

The Fourier transform is normalized by $\widehat{f}(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) e^{-2\pi i x \xi}\,dx$.

Question: Suppose $\psi$ is an orthonormal wavelet such that $\psi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$. Must the Fourier transform $\widehat{\psi}$ necessarily be compactly supported?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of the question whether every Schwartz-class orthonormal wavelet on $\mathbb{R}$ (dyadic dilations) must have compactly supported Fourier transform. Known constructions of well-localized wavelets (e.g., Meyer wavelets) yield Schwartz wavelets with band-limited Fourier transform, but the converse necessity does not appear to be established in the sources found. Status appears to remain open, but no authoritative source was located to confirm this conclusively.

status_evidence.title: Orthonormal Bases of Compactly Supported Wavelets — Daubechies
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs compactly supported orthonormal wavelets with prescribed regularity, but such wavelets are not in the Schwartz class.
status_evidence.claim: Compactly supported smooth wavelets exist but are not Schwartz; does not address the converse question.

status_evidence.title: Compactly supported tight wavelet frames and orthonormal wavelets of exponential decay
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses existence of well-localized orthonormal wavelets with various decay/support properties.
status_evidence.claim: Standard literature treats Schwartz/band-limited (Meyer-type) and compactly supported (Daubechies-type) wavelets as separate families, without resolving whether Schwartz forces band-limited.
